title: Far From Home
subtitle: Luebeck. 28 days. 20 euros.
about: STORYBOARD AND SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for prose, branching, economy deltas,
UI/mechanic unlocks and pacing. story.ink and story.twee predate it and no longer
match; treat them as historical until regenerated from this file.
JSON has no comments, so commentary lives in real fields: beat, econ_note, sets_note, about.
NOT A LANGUAGE-LEARNING GAME. No scene teaches German and no scene may claim to.
NO RECORDED AUDIO EXISTS. The audio[] arrays are advisory ambience slots for the
procedural SFX layer, never asset filenames. The pick loop's cue is the VISUAL gender
rail pulse. See Docs/STORY_FORMAT.md before editing anything in this file.

shape.rule: Introduce mechanics on the widening half. Master them on the narrowing half.

acts.name: One thread
acts.intent: Arrival, one conversation, and the der/die/das ramp. Ends on the Aha.

acts.name: Two threads
acts.intent: The Kaution fork: pay it and be broke, or borrow and keep a runway.

acts.name: Four to six threads
acts.intent: Every remaining system arrives here. Peak chaos.

acts.name: Threads close
acts.intent: Nothing new is introduced. Mastery and untangling only.

acts.name: One thread
acts.intent: One desk, one stamp, three shadings of the same ending.

pacing.rule_source: Docs/THE_MAKING_OF.md section 10 (the 90s target is withdrawn; budget_s is kept as a measuring instrument, not a goal)

delivery_modes.overlay: narration plays over live gameplay and never blocks input
delivery_modes.blocking: a real conversation; the dialogue IS the interaction
delivery_modes.gameplay: a minigame owns the screen; narration is incidental

pacing.note: The 90s budget is the time to the Aha, not the length of Act I. The critical path reaches shift_3_test at 167s, and that is a DELIBERATE design divergence: this is a slow-burn narrative sim, and compressing the Luebeck arrival to satisfy a stopwatch makes the pick loop a colour-matching game with nothing at stake. First interactive scene is at 10s, which is what the Engagement criterion actually asks for. Reasoning: Docs/THE_MAKING_OF.md section 10. Do NOT retune durations or budget_s to make this pass, and do NOT point quickstart at shift_3_test - that was tried, reverted, and is now pinned by assertions in build/verify.js. quickstart lands on shift_1_teach, where the mechanic is taught.

economy_ref: src/core/economy.js is authoritative; Docs/CANONICAL_NUMBERS.md mirrors it

Pink. Middle. Gone. Blue. Bottom. Gone. You are not reading. You are moving.

payout.formula: trial rate: baseWage 13.00 + accuracy 7.50 - trial deduction 9.25 = 11.25 net
payout.note: Act I is ONE evening shift shown in three ramp stages, so it pays ONCE, here. The trial deduction is the joke and it is also what keeps the player near 30 EUR for the Act II Kaution fork. Later shifts use the real engine payout (wallet + pay).

prose: You stand on the pavement between the two buildings, which are four hundred metres apart, and you do the loop again in your head to check.

prose: Outside it is cold and completely bright.
You have {wallet}€, a body at {body}, a residence permit valid for three years, and a folder that cost eighty cents.
You walk back through the Marktplatz and you know the names of eleven people between here and the WG, and four of them wave.
Martha bangs on the bakery window with the flat of her hand and points at the oven, which means sit down, which means she has already put something on a plate.
You came here four weeks ago with twenty euros and it turns out that was never the number that mattered.
THE END - "Angekommen." Arrived.
You walk back through the Marktplatz. You made it. Every single number came out right and the folder is full and the stamp is real.
You pass the bakery and Martha is in the window and you nod, and she nods, and you keep walking because there is a shift at six.
You have the visa. Three years. You will work out the rest of it in the second one.
THE END - "Geschafft." Managed it.
You walk back through the Marktplatz and you cannot feel very much about it.
The stamp is real. The permit is three years. You beat every number and the numbers were the only thing you spoke to for two of those four weeks.
Klaus was on his crate for fourteen years and he was somebody's friend for none of them. You put the folder in your bag and you think about that all the way home.
Three years is a long time. Long enough to do it differently.
THE END - "Ueberlebt." Survived.
